title: Cumulus AI onboarding launch & data residency sync

Dedicated trial provisioning and capacity sizing

transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-16 14:30 PDT - Duration: ~58m
Attendees: Jordan Ellis (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood CSM), Marco Li (Redwood SE), Aisha Khan (CTO, Cumulus AI), Daniel Park (Head of ML Ops), Maria Lopez (Security Lead), Tom Watson (Platform Eng)

Summary: quick kickoff to align on onboarding timeline, data residency needs (EU only for certain datasets), and POC scope - latency + cost for inference.

00:00 Jordan: alright hi everyone, thanks for joining, um this is Jordan from Redwood Inference. quick intros?
00:08 Aisha: hi I'm Aisha, CTO at Cumulus, we run multi-tenant models for forecasting, mostly EU data reqs, thanks for doing this.
00:14 Daniel: Daniel, ML Ops, I'll be hands on for the benchmarks and infra.
00:17 Maria: Maria, security, I'll own compliance questions.
00:20 Tom: Tom, platform, networking and access.
00:22 Jordan: and on our side Priya is the CSM, Marco our SE. We wanted to start with high level requirements then move into network and POC plan.
00:33 Marco: yeah, and just to set expectations — we can support hosted and dedicated and private deployments. Given you mentioned EU data-only requirement, we'll talk about VPC/private options and Dedicated capacity that can be regionalized.
00:45 Aisha: yeah the main constraint is that a subset of our customer data must never leave eu-west-1, so residency and audit logs are big. we may still evaluate hosted for non-sensitive traffic.
00:56 Maria: also we need audit log retention for 7 years, and we use a corporate KMS (Azure KeyVault) for at-rest keys. can you support external key management/bring-your-own-key?
01:07 Marco: short answer: yes. our Private and Dedicated options support KMS integrations; we also have a customer-managed key flow for Private deployments. i'll follow up with the integration note, but the flow is standard - we don't store plaintext keys.
01:20 Maria: okay, was the KMS flow documented? sometimes the wording in the doc is different.
01:24 Jordan: we'll send the KMS integration doc and the network diagram after this call, plus SOC 2 artifact.
01:29 Daniel: great. on the workload side we have a lot of short synchronous calls, 200ms p50 target ideally, and throughput about 80 concurrent requests during peak. what's realistic on your side?
01:40 Marco: for that profile we usually recommend a small Dedicated pool with gpus sized for low-latency, plus caching to cut repeated prefixes. for 200ms p50 we'll want to do benchmarks with your prompt length distribution. the runtime picks kernels and batching based on sequence length — um, sometimes the automatic batching adds latency if sequences vary a lot.
01:56 Tom: when you say caching, you mean KV cache? sometimes I see it written as K-V cash in the notes — just checking.
02:02 Marco: (laughs) yes, KV cache, not K-V cash. it stores key value kv states per request so repeated prefixes can be served much faster.
02:08 Aisha: okay, for the POC we'll provide representative prompts and expected concurrency.
02:12 Jordan: perfect. let's agree a POC: two-week Dedicated trial in eu-west-1, run three benchmark runs (latency, throughput, cost), and a security deep-dive. agree?
02:22 Aisha: yes. timeline — we want production decision by mid-April. so a two-week POC this month fits.
02:28 Priya: i'll open a staging project and request the Dedicated trial provisioning; Marco will run the initial benchmarks once they share sample prompts and a test harness.
02:36 Daniel: question on data in transit — does Redwood's hosted API route through any US hops if I pick eu-west-1? we need to ensure the path remains regional.
02:45 Marco: usually our routing keeps requests regional when pinned, but there are rare control-plane calls to other regions. for Private deployments the control plane can be customer-managed in VPC which avoids that. we'll include the exact network flow map in the diagram.
02:58 Maria: also need to confirm log retention and where audit logs live. do they go to your cloud account or can we ship them to our SIEM?
03:06 Jordan: we support forwarding audit logs to your SIEM (e.g., Splunk) and can adjust retention. for Dedicated and Private, customers typically push logs to their own storage.
03:15 Maria: okay good. can you support SAML SSO and RBAC? we need scoped roles for platform, sec, and devs.
03:23 Priya: yes we support SAML/SSO, provisioning via SCIM is on the roadmap but not GA for all plans — we'll note which fields require manual steps.
03:31 Tom: networking wise we'll need a list of IP ranges to allow and a staging VPC peering plan.
03:36 Jordan: i'll include the allowlist and a sample peering topology.
03:40 Aisha: competitor question — we've also been talking to Anthropic and a managed provider, they emphasize model quality but have custom infra costs. how do you compare for TCO?
03:50 Marco: high level — we focus on serving economics: with batching, KV caching, and quantization suggestions we can often cut token cost by 30-50% compared to off-the-shelf hosting. for fair comparison we'll run cost-per-100k-requests in the POC.
04:05 Daniel: can you run same prompt set on a 13B and 70B model to show cost/delta?
04:10 Marco: yep, we can include a small matrix — we'll also show quantization profiles if you'd like. note that for strict EU residency we may need to use model artifacts hosted in region or Private deployment to avoid cross-region model pulls.
04:25 Maria: SOC2 and encryption at rest — do you have enveloping with customer key?
04:29 Jordan: yes, envelope encryption with customer-managed KMS is supported for Private and Dedicated; we'll send the exact architecture doc.
04:36 Tom: what's the expected ETA to provision a small Dedicated pool? days or weeks?
04:40 Marco: typically 2-5 business days for small pool in a supported region, faster if capacity is available — we'll try to get eu-west-1 within 48-72 hours but can't promise until we see capacity.
04:51 Aisha: ok that works. next steps recap?
04:54 Priya: action items: we'll provision a staging project and request Dedicated trial, Jordan to send SOC2 + network diagram + KMS note, Marco to schedule and run benchmarks once prompts are in, Cumulus to share sample prompt set and allowlist.
05:10 Daniel: note about performance tests — we'll use a closed harness with 500 concurrent clients to simulate burst.
05:16 Marco: great, please also include typical sequence length distribution and tokenization details.
05:22 Maria: and i'll schedule a security-only follow-up next Thursday for KMS and log retention specifics.
05:27 Jordan: sounds good. Jordan: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the docs and the staging invite by tomorrow.
05:33 Aisha: thanks all.

Links referenced: onboarding runbook (link: https://redwood.example.com/onboarding/runbook), SOC2 artifact (link to secure doc), KMS integration note (link: /docs/kms-integration), benchmark spreadsheet template (link).

Recap (end): POC two-week Dedicated trial in eu-west-1, provide sample prompts and allowlist, run latency/throughput/cost benchmark, security deep-dive with Maria next Thursday.
